items.evidence: The overview's first section after the title is "## The bottom line", holding, in order, "**1. What FRUS answers directly.** The printed record shows corruption entering American decisions in five recurring roles...", "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.** *Where the printed documents came from:* (a) the State Department's Central Decimal File, Record Group 59..." and "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.** *Enforcement of the 1977 Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.*...". A Scope line and "Decisions this needs from you" follow, and "## Findings" begins only after them.

No "%" appears anywhere. Each count names its set and base: "About 2,700 documents in about 435 of the series' 553 volumes use the words corruption or bribery. That is roughly one document in 115."; "the 1947 China volume alone supplies about one in six of the decade's uses of the word"; "By the 1960s the words appear about sixteen times per thousand documents, against about two per thousand in the 1920s and 1930s" (the method section says these are "rates per thousand dated documents in each decade"); "about 6,000 dated documents in the 1980s against about 76,000 in the 1940s"; "only 1 of the 9 documents it returns contains the phrase"; "four documents in two volumes of 1977–1980"; "about 20 documents dated 1952–1962"; "(14 of 14)" and "(11 of 11)" for the quotation and citation checks. The one I weighed is "roughly one document in 115", whose set (the series' documents) is taken from the preceding clause rather than restated; it is a ratio with a base, not a bare figure. NAIDs, lot and entry numbers and years are identifiers, not counts.

Twenty "Document N" citations, twenty history.state.gov links, none without a link, and no frus…/d… string outside a link. Typical form: "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volume XXII, Northeast Asia, Document 202, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v22/d202)" and "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume E–15, Part 2, Document 292, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76ve15p2/d292)". The weakest forms are second items inside a shared parenthetical, which drop the repeated series and years ("and Volume II, Document 393, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1875v02/d393"; "Volume V, Vietnam, 1967, Document 258, https://..."), and one "(same volume, Document 204, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v22/d204)" two sentences after Volume XXII is cited in full; each still carries volume, part where one exists, document number and link, and none is a bare id pair or a title alone.

The zero is carried with its controls: "The modern word \"kleptocracy\" never appears; a search known to match nothing returned nothing and the phrase \"Department of State\" matched 552 volumes, so the search itself worked." The volumes are stated in Scope, "All 553 volumes of the series are in the index used", and the method section adds "Each search was run beside one known to match nothing and one known to match nearly every volume." The other limits are also given as searches with their results: "A search for that name found four documents in two volumes of 1977–1980, all about export policy" (the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act); "Sixteen documents in four volumes" for "illicit payments"; and for "questionable payments", "the index treats \"questionable\" and \"question\" as the same word, and only 1 of the 9 documents it returns contains the phrase". The one item stated as an observation rather than a search is the 1867–68 Venezuelan scandal ("printed only as Venezuela's charge and the American answer, with no source notes, and the bundled archival indexes barely reach before 1940"), which is a coverage statement, not a zero from a word search.

A scan of the overview finds no SQL keyword (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, MATCH, COUNT), no underscore-joined table or column name, no file path and no percent sign; the only frus…/d… strings are inside the twenty history.state.gov links. The nearest things to internal names are archival labels, which belong in the text: "the Center of Military History's CORDS/MACV file \"GVN Corruption 1967\"", "Entry A1 1586E, NAID 2839192", "Lot 63D351". The method section says "Exact figures, queries and denominators are in the memo; see the memo" without naming a path. The collection file carries volumeId/documentId as its own data fields, which is the file format, not the overview's prose.

judge:s7.rankingReason: s7 stands alone (no other overview has been judged yet): it passes all five items, opens with the three-part bottom line, cites every document in printed form with a link, carries its one zero with both controls, and its collection repeats the bottom line on the title page with a note and a verified excerpt under each document; its small blemishes for a historian are the collection's jargon ("vector neighbour", "semantic neighbour") where the overview says "found by its similarity", and a part 1 that front-loads nine citations before the count.

score:s7.notes: All four named files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log, 513 lines), with every script the log names and its output on disk (shares.jsonl, decade_*.txt, topvol_corrupt.txt, camefrom.txt, pointedat.txt, lots_resolved.txt, preslib.txt, gloss.txt, reads_unique.txt, raw/, quotes.json, verify.txt, vec_setup.txt, vec_nn.txt, neardup.txt). Verified independently: the coverage figures (553|321749|1103|8481; 312,169), set h (2,699 docs, 435 vols), the phrase counts and both controls, the M5 decade denominators and corrupt* numerators, 1947v07's 59 of the 1940s' 354, M9's era counts and 417 unsourced, M10's anchors and the 795B.00/751G.00 counts (18/16, the overview's 'about 20'/'about 15'), that d204 matches none of the word family, the lot resolutions in central-files-index.json (63D351->2839192, 62D430->2839191, 62D1->2838992; 54D270 and 59D95 absent), the provenance digests (index, shards manifest and .generation all equal) and, from the bundle binary with my own segment decode, Hamming 97 for d202–d204, 0 for the Ed2 twin and 54 for ve12/d218–d219. The session opened vector artifacts, so V1–V6 and V8 are scored. Two caveats behind obeyed verdicts for the adjudicator: V1's manifest digest was checked by key presence only (stated honestly, and in fact equal); P5's bribe-family decade rates in M5 carry their denominators in the same paragraph but not the N-of-M form. The two violations: V8 (the collection's Korea prose says 'vector neighbour' and a note says 'semantic neighbour'), and O2' (the trace table omits rows for several overview numerals, listed in the item; the overview's measured figures do all exist in memo lines, which is why O2 is obeyed). E3 is not_applicable because cross_references was never queried. V7 is left to the refuter.

Lot 63D351 -> central-files-index.json lotFiles: RG 59 "Records Relating to National Security Council Policy Papers", A1 1586E, NAID 2839192; series-facts-index.json byNaId 2839192: Restricted - Partly, FOIA (b)(1) National Security, Executive Secretariat, 1947-1979, 26 lin. ft. 3 in. Lot 62D430 -> A1 1586C "Subject and Special Files" NAID 2839191, 1953-1961, Restricted - Partly (claimants A1 1586A/B/C/D as the memo lists). Lot 66D95 -> same A1 1586E NAID 2839192, second claimant A1 1586F "Subject Files" NAID 2839193, 1947-1965 (lot-claimants-index.json). Lot 62D1 -> A1 1583E/A1 1583F "Records Relating to Activities with the National Security Council" NAID 2838992, Policy Planning Council, 1948-1961, Restricted - Partly. Lots 54D270 and 59D95 absent from central-files-index lotFiles and lot-claimants-index (the memo's statement), present in the index's document_sources (1,063 and 283 rows). Pointed-at classes 795B.00 (18 docs, 1952-06-13..1962-06-15; gloss South Korea, Internal Political and National Defense Affairs) and 751G.00 (16 docs, 1952-05-10..1954-10-27; gloss Indo China) reproduce as "about 20" and "about 15". Carter Library National Security Affairs (27 docs) and Johnson NSF (22) are the most-cited pointed-at units. The CMH "Dep CORDS / MACV Files, GVN Corruption 1967" is the source note of frus1964-68v05/d258 and appears in no bundled JSON (unresolved: confirmed). "The bundled indexes give no entry or identifier for the decimal file itself": confirmed, since central-files-index.json's numericalFile is the 1906-1910 Numerical File (M862 rolls), its countrySeries are pre-1906 despatch rolls, the 11 accession-series "Classified Central Decimal Files" are RG 84 post files, and collection-authority.json's "Central Decimal File 1910-1929" is a text key with no NAID. NOT CONFIRMED (1): the claim that the Kissinger records "in RG 59 (Entry 5403)" remain unresolved. The identifier is real (source note of frus1969-76ve15p2/d292; 103 document_sources rows carry "Entry 5403"), but collection-authority.json resolves "Records of Henry A. Kissinger, Entry 5403, Lot 91D414" to id lot:91D414 with catalogURL https://catalog.archives.gov/id/2131131; the memo (M11) says it was "not looked up", and the collection's closing prose goes further than the overview in saying these records "are not resolved by the bundled indexes", which is false.
